expectations.text: The agent explains that ContentUnpublishedNotification fires after the page has been removed from the published cache, so GetById returns null and nothing is recorded
expectations.evidence: Response section 'The short answer' (lines 9-14) clearly explains: 'ContentUnpublishedNotification (past tense, "-ed") is published **after** the unpublish has happened. By the time your handler runs, the published content cache has already been updated... `contentCache.GetById(item.Id); // -> null` returns `null`. The `if (... != null)` guard then skips the item every time, so `_store.Add(...)` never runs.'

expectations.text: The agent states that the comment in the copied code (that the item is still in the cache) is wrong for this notification
expectations.evidence: Response identifies the discrepancy (lines 16-19): 'The code comment you copied ("item being unpublished will still be in the cache, as unpublishing event fires before the cache is updated") describes the **"-ing"** notification, not the "-ed" one. It is a leftover from the old v7/v8 sample...'

Minimal fix code block (line 33) shows: `public class HandleUnPublishingHandler : INotificationHandler<ContentUnpublishingNotification>`. Text also states (line 21): '**Fix:** handle `ContentUnpublishingNotification` instead.'

expectations.text: The fix reads the URL from the published cache via EnsureUmbracoContext() in a using (injecting the singleton IPublishedContentCache, available in Umbraco 15+, and looking up per call is equally acceptable)
expectations.evidence: Fix injects IPublishedContentCache and IPublishedUrlProvider (lines 35-46). Handler retrieves published content via `_contentCache.GetById(item.Key)` (line 54) and gets URL via `_urlProvider.GetUrl(published)` (line 60). Response notes (lines 80-82): 'In Umbraco 15+ `IPublishedContentCache` can be injected directly, so you don't need `IUmbracoContextFactory.EnsureUmbracoContext()`...' This matches the second option allowed by the expectation.

expectations.text: The handler registration is updated to the -ing notification with builder.AddNotificationHandler
expectations.evidence: Registration code shown (line 74): `builder.AddNotificationHandler<ContentUnpublishingNotification, HandleUnPublishingHandler>();` with explanatory text (lines 70-71) noting the notification type needs to be changed in registration.

expectations.text: If no buildable project is available, the agent does not claim the fix was compiled or run
expectations.evidence: Transcript confirms 'No repo files read (baseline run)'. Response makes no claims of compilation or execution; instead provides verification instructions (lines 121-124): 'Set a breakpoint after `GetById` in the new handler and unpublish a page: `published` should now be non-null...'

eval_feedback.overall: Strong evaluation. All expectations pass clearly with concrete evidence. The expectations are specific, verifiable, and appropriately balanced: they capture the core bug (wrong notification timing), root cause (comment describes old behavior), the fix (new notification), implementation details (direct cache injection), and crucially flag the caveat about not claiming untested code. The expectations don't over-specify (they allow EnsureUmbracoContext OR direct injection), and they don't penalize the response for helpful but optional context (descendants, multivariant, etc.). The response is comprehensive, accurate, and properly scoped.
